extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — grant applicants, investigators, institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: A news roundup of NIH extramural policy, process, and resource updates intended to inform applicants and awardees about changes that affect grant preparation, review, and compliance. Covers topics like model selection, data management plans, reproducibility, review scoring categories, and programmatic changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models (NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing studies, choose models (including New Approach Methodologies) that are scientifically appropriate for the specific research question, balance human relevance and translational potential, and justify model selection in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects format
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants for PF5 should view the overview to learn the PF5 application format, structural features, and the possibility that applications could be split into linked awards after peer review; follow the described format and prepare for linked-award scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans in 2026, use the newly issued pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified by NIH; adhere to the updated structure rather than older templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider and document how their proposed work promotes replication and reproducibility (study design, methods, analyses, documentation, sharing) and be aware of the new initiative and any Highlighted Topic requests that incentivize these efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' score
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application receives the 'competitive but not discussed' designation, understand this reflects placement in the middle third after a cut-off and does not necessarily indicate a weak application; use NIH guidance to interpret next steps (e.g., resubmission strategy, Just-in-Time procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of centralized NIH peer review changes
rubrics_metrics.description: In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR). One year later NIH reports the consolidation is strengthening efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and administrators should account for the centralized CSR peer-review process when preparing submissions (timelines, review expectations) and stay informed about how consolidation may affect study section behavior, scoring, and administrative processes.
